title: Custom bridge networks
idea: A custom bridge is a private network you create yourself. Containers on it find each other by name; containers on other networks cannot reach them directly.
points: `docker network create bookstore-net` makes a custom bridge network.
Join it with `--network bookstore-net`, or attach a running container with `docker network connect`.
Docker's built-in DNS resolves container names on the same custom network.
Containers on different networks cannot reach each other directly; a network is a boundary.

steps.caption: `docker network create bookstore-net` makes the network. `--network bookstore-net` puts `tool` and `api` on it.
`tool` calls `api` by name. Docker's built-in DNS turns the name into the container's IP address.
`job` sits on the default bridge, a different network, so it cannot reach `api`.
`docker network connect bookstore-net job` adds the running container to the network. Now `job` reaches `api` by name.

code.caption: Create a network, start the API on it, and reach it by name from inside and outside.

walk.text: Create a custom bridge network named `bookstore-net`.
Start the API on it. `--network` goes before the image name.
A one-off Alpine container on the same network pings `api` by name. It works.
Start `job` with no `--network`: it joins the default bridge.
From `job`, ping `api` by name. It fails: another network, and no name lookup.
Attach the running `job` to `bookstore-net`. No restart needed.
Ping again. The name now resolves.

pitfalls: Add `--network` to every `docker run`; one without it lands on the default bridge.
Do not publish a port just so containers can talk; on one network they already can.
Share a network only with containers that should talk; all ports are open between them.

quiz.q: `api` and `tool` are on `bookstore-net`; `job` is on the default bridge. Which call works?
quiz.why: Name lookup works only inside a custom network, and different networks are isolated. `tool` and `api` share one.

takeaway: Create one custom bridge per app; its containers find each other by name.
